title: The Turing test measures judges as much as machines
body: Turing proposed imitation as an operational stand-in for 'can machines think' in 1950, partly to dodge definitional swamps. Chatbots from ELIZA onward showed how readily people project understanding onto fluent text. The test's history is therefore double: progress in machines, and a mirror held up to human credulity, which turns out to be the easier variable.
